bottleneck: Even with complete wiring diagrams, structure does not predict function: C. elegans' fully mapped 302-neuron connectome still cannot explain all its behavior, because neuromodulation, extrasynaptic signaling, and dynamic network states are invisible in the wiring. Researchers found neurons communicating beyond their anatomical connections, and the same circuit produces different behaviors depending on modulatory context. The connectome is the skeleton; the software running on it — dynamics, plasticity, modulation — remains unmapped, and no theory derives function from structure plus dynamics.
current_state: The field is shifting from pure connectomics to combined structure-function mapping, but no framework yet derives behavior from wiring plus dynamics. The gap is acknowledged as the central challenge.

title: Connectome structure fails to predict behavior
why_it_blocks: If wiring diagrams cannot explain a 302-neuron worm, they will not explain 86 billion human neurons. The structure-function gap threatens to make connectomics an expensive atlas without a theory, consuming resources that dynamics research needs.
